name: Apple-Pear Crumble
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Core and slice the apples and the pear into thin wedges.
Smear a little of the butter over the bottom of a small baking dish.
Toss the apples and the pear with the sugar and the ground cinnamon, then spread them in the dish.
Rub the remaining butter into the all-purpose flour, brown sugar, rolled oats, and salt until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.
Scatter that crumb mix evenly over the fruit.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the fruit is bubbling at the edges and the top has turned light brown.
Cool 10 minutes so the juices thicken before spooning out portions.

attribution.note: Renamed from the compote to Apple-Pear Crumble. Scaled to 4 servings from a larger casserole, using 2 apples and 1 pear. Chose butter rather than margarine. Optional sugar and cinnamon were kept. A pinch of sugar, a pinch of cinnamon, and a dash of salt follow the page.

name: Bangers and Mash
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into chunks about 3/4 inch thick.
Warm the vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat. Lay the pork sausages in one layer and brown them about 2 minutes on each side.
Drop the heat to low and keep turning the pork sausages every few minutes for 25 minutes. They are done when the center is no longer pink and a thermometer in the middle of a link reads 160°F (71°C).
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water for about 15 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.
Drain the potatoes well and return them to the warm pot off the heat.
Mash the potatoes with the butter and the milk until smooth.
Spoon the mash onto plates and set the pork sausages alongside.

attribution.note: Two sausages and two potatoes per person for 4 servings. The page left oil, butter, and milk unmeasured; set to 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 2 tbsp butter, and 1/4 cup milk. Sausages are cooked to 160°F (71°C) with no pink remaining.

name: Classic Tourtière
steps: Dice the onion and the potato. Mince the garlic.
Cut the butter into the all-purpose flour with 1/2 tsp of the salt. Sprinkle in the cold water and gather a soft dough. Divide it in half, wrap, and chill while the filling cooks.
In a wide pot, cook the onion and garlic with a spoon of the filling juices from the meat as it starts to render, about 4 minutes over medium heat.
Add the ground pork and the ground beef. Break them up and cook until the mix reaches 160°F (71°C), about 12 minutes.
Stir in the potato, the remaining salt, the black pepper, the ground cloves, the dried savory, the cinnamon, and the water. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, until the potato is soft. Cool 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with one dough round, fill it, and cover with the second round. Crimp the edge and cut three vents.
Bake 40 minutes, until the crust is deep gold. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

attribution.note: No tourtière page in the Wikibooks cookbook category.

name: Shepherd's Pie
steps: Peel and chunk the potatoes. Boil them about 20 minutes, until a knife meets no resistance.
Dice the onion. Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a skillet and cook the onion with a pinch of the salt until it turns clear, about 6 minutes.
In a separate pan, melt the lard and brown the ground lamb over medium-high heat, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion, the mixed herbs, and the black pepper to the lamb. Sprinkle on the all-purpose flour and stir for 3 minutes.
Pour in the beef stock. Simmer 30 minutes, then cook uncovered a few minutes more until the liquid sits level with the meat. The lamb should be at least 160°F (71°C).
Drain the potatoes. Mash with the remaining butter, the rest of the salt, and the milk until creamy rather than stiff.
Spread the meat in a shallow baking dish, cover with the mash, and rough the surface with a fork.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 35 minutes, until the potato peaks are golden.

attribution.note: Lamb was chosen from the page's lamb-or-beef line. Optional cheese, mixed vegetables, and extra lard were left out; 1 tbsp lard is the browning fat. Mixed herbs, milk, butter, salt, and black pepper were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp, 1/2 cup, 3 tbsp, 1 tsp, and 1/2 tsp. Ground lamb is cooked to 160°F (71°C). The 1 lb meat and 3 lb potatoes match about 6 servings.

name: Weeknight Butter Chicken
steps: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-size cubes. Juice the lemon.
Toss the chicken thighs with the tandoori masala, the unsweetened yogurt, and the lemon juice until every piece is coated. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Slice the onion thin. Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion with the cinnamon until the onion softens and picks up a little color, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, the ginger, the ground turmeric, the chile powder, and the ground coriander. Cook 1 minute.
Add the marinated chicken thighs and stir until the meat is white on the outside, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and the cream. Cover and simmer 12 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the chicken thighs read 165°F (74°C) in the center.

attribution.note: Reworded from Indian Butter Chicken I. Optional cinnamon was kept. The 30-minute yogurt rest is included in the 55 minutes. Chicken is cooked to 165°F (74°C). Amounts sit in the page's ranges (1 lb thighs, 2 tsp chile powder, 150 g tomato paste) for 4 servings.

name: Montreal Smoked Meat Sandwich
steps: Set a steamer basket over an inch of simmering water, or use a covered skillet with a splash of water.
Pile the montreal smoked meat in the basket, cover, and steam 6 minutes, until the slices are hot and the edges curl.
Butter one side of each slice of rye bread.
Warm a griddle over medium heat and toast the rye bread, buttered side down, about 2 minutes.
Spread the yellow mustard on the untoasted sides.
Stack the montreal smoked meat and the dill pickle on four slices, close the sandwiches, and cut them in half.

attribution.note: No Montreal smoked-meat sandwich page. Montreal Steak Seasoning is a spice mix and was not cited.

name: Toronto Peameal Bacon Sandwich
steps: Cut the peameal bacon into 1/4-inch slices if it is still in a slab.
Split the kaiser rolls and warm them, cut side down, in a dry skillet for 1 minute.
Film a skillet with the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Fry the peameal bacon 3 minutes per side, until browned and 145°F (63°C) in the center. Rest the slices 3 minutes.
Grind the black pepper over the peameal bacon.
Spread the yellow mustard on the kaiser rolls, pile in the peameal bacon, and close the sandwiches.

attribution.note: No peameal bacon sandwich page.

name: Weeknight Shortcut Poutine
steps: Cut the potatoes into finger-thick sticks and rinse them until the water runs clearer. Pat them dry.
Pour the poutine sauce into a small pot and warm it over low heat so it loosens slowly.
Heat the vegetable oil to 365°F (185°C) in a deep pot.
Fry the potatoes in two batches for 5 minutes, until they are cooked through but still pale. Drain them.
Return the potatoes to the oil for about 1 minute, until the outsides are crisp and golden. Drain again.
Heap the potatoes in a serving dish, scatter the cheese curds over them, and pour the hot poutine sauce on top before the cheese curds fully melt.

attribution.note: Reworded. Chose canned poutine sauce rather than gravy. The 1 L of vegetable oil, 5 potatoes, and 2 cups of cheese curds match about 4 servings. Cheese curds stay cold until the sauce goes on.

name: Canadian Split Pea Soup
steps: Soak the yellow split peas overnight, then drain them. This soak is not counted in the cooking time.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roast the ham hocks 35 minutes, turning once, until the rind is browned.
Halve one onion. Cut one carrot and one stalk of celery into large chunks. Put them in a pot with the ham hocks, 2 sprigs of the fresh thyme, the bay leaf, the black peppercorns, and the water.
Bring the pot to a boil, skim the foam, and simmer 3 hours, until the ham hocks are tender.
Lift out the ham hocks. Strain the broth and discard the spent vegetables. Pull the meat off the bones in bite-size pieces.

Dice the remaining onion, the remaining carrot, and the remaining celery. Mince the garlic. Return the broth to the pot with the yellow split peas, the diced vegetables, the garlic, and the leaves from the last sprig of fresh thyme.
Simmer 70 minutes, until the yellow split peas collapse. Stir in the ham, the salt, and the black pepper and simmer 10 minutes more.
Ladle into bowls, add the parsley, and finish with the olive oil.

attribution.note: Reworded. Overnight pea soak is excluded from the 330 minutes. Optional celery is included; optional miso is left out. Salt and black pepper were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp and 1/2 tsp. Olive oil was chosen over canola for the drizzle. Two hocks at about 2 lb total suit 8 servings.

name: Maple-Glazed Salmon
steps: Soak a cedar plank in water for several hours. That soak is not included in the 40 minutes.
Stir 2 tbsp of the lemon juice with the grapeseed oil, the dried rosemary, the maple syrup, and 3/4 tsp of the chipotle powder.
Coat the salmon fillets with that mix and let them stand 20 minutes. Slice the scallions thin.
Combine what is left of the lemon juice with the last of the chipotle powder and hold that small bowl for the table.
Heat a grill to medium-high. Lay the soaked plank on the grate, lid down, for 2 minutes. Scatter half the salt on the plank.

Set the salmon fillets on the plank, skin side down if they have skin. Turn the grill to low, close the lid, and cook about 15 minutes, until the center of each fillet is 145°F (63°C) and the flesh flakes.
Move the salmon fillets to a platter, scatter the scallions and the rest of the salt over them, and serve the reserved lemon-chipotle mix alongside.

attribution.note: Salmon is cooked to 145°F (63°C). The plank soak of several hours is excluded from the time, like a marinade. Salt was unmeasured and set to 1 tsp. The lemon juice and chipotle powder are split between the glaze and a small finishing sauce.

name: Chipotle Maple Pork Tenderloin
steps: Trim the pork tenderloin. Stir the lime juice, the lime zest, the garlic powder, the salt, the black pepper, and the honey. Coat the pork tenderloin, seal it, and refrigerate 24 hours. That rest is not included in the 35 minutes.
Mince the chipotle chiles and stir them into the maple syrup.
Lift the pork tenderloin out of the marinade and pat it dry. Discard the used marinade.
Heat a grill. Oil the grate with the oil.
Sear the pork tenderloin over the hottest area, turning every couple of minutes, until the thickest point reads 145°F (63°C), about 16 to 20 minutes.
Set the pork tenderloin on foil, pour the chipotle-maple syrup mix over it, and wrap loosely.
Rest 5 minutes, which covers the 3-minute rest, then slice and spoon the glaze over the meat.

attribution.note: Maple-Dijon chops had no page; this is the chipotle maple pork from the source. The 24-hour marinade is excluded from the 35 minutes. The page stopped at 140°F; this version cooks the tenderloin to 145°F (63°C) and rests it 5 minutes. Oil for the grate was not listed and 1 tbsp was added so the meat can sear.

name: Dutch-Oven Pot Roast
steps: Pat the bottom round roast dry and season it with the salt and the black pepper. Peel and chunk the carrots. Dice the onion. Quarter the red-skinned potatoes. Mince the garlic. Chop the rosemary, the thyme, and the oregano.
Heat 1/4 cup of the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the bottom round roast on all sides, about 12 minutes. Move it to a plate.
Add the rest of the olive oil with the carrots, the onion, and the red-skinned potatoes. Cook until the onion edges brown, about 8 minutes. Scoop the vegetables out.
Pour in the beef broth, the red wine, the tomato juice, and the balsamic vinegar. Scrape up the browned bits. Stir in the garlic, the rosemary, the thyme, and the oregano.
Whisk the all-purpose flour with a ladle of that liquid, then stir it back into the pot so the sauce can thicken.
Return the vegetables and the bottom round roast to the pot. Cover and bake at 325°F (165°C) for about 3 hours, until a fork slides into the beef with little resistance.
Let the pot stand 10 minutes, then slice the bottom round roast and spoon the vegetables and sauce over it.

attribution.note: Beef is braised until fork-tender. Salt and black pepper were unmeasured and set to 2 tsp and 1 tsp. The page's 225°F oven for 6 hours was raised to 325°F so the liquid simmers; plan on about 3 hours. Flour is the higher end of the page's range. A 2 1/2 lb roast suits 6 servings.

name: Hearty Beef Stew
steps: Cut the beef into 1-inch chunks. Toss the beef with the all-purpose flour until coated.
Heat the oil in a wide pot. Brown the beef in batches over medium-high heat, about 4 minutes per batch.
Return all the beef to the pot. Add the bay leaf, the marjoram, the oregano, the tomato juice, the beef broth, the salt, and the black pepper.
Cover and simmer 60 minutes, stirring often so the beef does not catch. It should be starting to soften.
Peel the carrots and cut them, the potatoes, and the celery into chunks about the size of the beef.
Add the carrots and simmer 15 minutes. Add the potatoes and the celery and simmer 15 minutes more, until the vegetables are soft but still hold their shape and the beef is fork-tender.
Discard the bay leaf before ladling the stew.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).

attribution.note: Reworded. A 2 lb pot matches about 6 servings, with 3 potatoes from the page's range of 2 to 4. Salt and black pepper were not on the ingredient list; 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper were added so the stew can be seasoned.

name: Country Roast Chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Take the giblets out of the chicken and pat the bird dry.
Loosen the skin over the breast. Rub the country roast chicken seasoning onto the meat under the skin and inside the cavity.
Slice one lemon thin and lay those slices in the roasting pan. Cut the other lemon into wedges.
Stuff the cavity with the rosemary, the thyme, and the lemon wedges. Set the chicken on the lemon slices.
Tuck 1 tbsp of the butter under the skin of each breast.
Roast until a thermometer in the thickest breast, not touching the butter, reads 165°F (74°C), about 65 minutes for a 3 lb bird.
Tent the chicken with foil and rest 10 minutes before carving.

attribution.note: The old title named root vegetables, which this page does not list, so the dish is Country Roast Chicken. A 3 lb chicken is shared across 6 servings. Butter under the skin means the dish is not dairy-free. Chicken is roasted to 165°F (74°C).

name: Sauerkraut Pierogi
steps: Stir 1/2 tsp of the salt into the all-purpose flour. Beat the egg and mix it in.
Add the water a spoon at a time until a soft dough forms that rolls without cracking. Knead briefly.
Squeeze extra moisture from the sauerkraut. Roll the dough on a floured board to cracker thickness.
Cut 3-inch rounds. Spoon sauerkraut onto each round, fold into a half-moon, and pinch the seam shut.
Boil a pot of water with the remaining salt. Drop in the dumplings and cook until they float, about 3 to 4 minutes. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the dumplings until both sides are golden, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve the dumplings while the butter is still glossy.

attribution.note: Shown as Sauerkraut Pierogi; the Wikibooks title is Pierogi II. The old title named sausage and caramelized onions, which this page does not list, so the dish is Pierogi II. Sauerkraut was chosen from the page's sauerkraut-or-cheese filling. The egg was kept. Water and butter were unmeasured and set to 1/2 cup and 3 tbsp. A 2-cup dough batch suits 4 servings.

name: Cabbage Rolls
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Soften the cabbage leaves in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Mix the ground beef, the milk, the egg, the cooked rice, the onion, the black pepper, and the salt. Divide into 12 mounds.
Wrap each mound in a cabbage leaf and pin the seam with a toothpick. Pack the rolls in a baking dish.
Stir the tomato paste, the chopped tomatoes, the sugar, the vinegar, and 1/2 cup of the water. Pour that sauce over the rolls.
Cover and bake about 55 minutes, until the center of a roll reads 160°F (71°C).
Lift the rolls out and pull the toothpicks. Whisk the cornstarch into the remaining 1/2 cup of water.
Stir that slurry into the sauce and warm it over medium heat until it thickens, about 3 minutes. Spoon the sauce over the rolls.

attribution.note: Reworded. The page's 40-minute bake was extended so the ground beef at the center reaches 160°F (71°C). The two 1/2-cup water measures on the page are combined as 1 cup and split between the sauce and the cornstarch. Twelve rolls suit 6 servings.

name: Classic Chicken Pot Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Let the pie crusts thaw if they are still firm.
Drain the mixed vegetables and the chicken.
Stir the cream of chicken soup, the cream of mushroom soup, the mixed vegetables, and the chicken in a bowl.
Fit one pie crust into a pie plate and pour in the filling.
Lay the second pie crust on top and press the rim to seal it.
Cut four slits in the top crust so steam can escape.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the crust is golden and the center of the filling is hot, 165°F (74°C).
Rest 8 minutes before slicing so the filling stays in the crust.

attribution.note: Reworded. Canned chicken is heated until the filling at the center is 165°F (74°C). Two crusts and the four cans suit about 6 servings.

name: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
steps: Boil the macaroni in salted water until tender, about 8 minutes. Drain it.
Warm the milk in a small pot until it steams.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the all-purpose flour and cook 1 minute.
Pour in the warm milk while whisking until the sauce is smooth and thickened, about 4 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cheddar cheese, the Parmesan cheese, and the cayenne pepper until the cheeses melt.
Fold the macaroni into the sauce until every piece is coated. Eat it from the pot; this version is not baked.

attribution.note: Stovetop method, matching the page. Scaled to about half for 4 servings (the page starts with 1 pound of macaroni). Parmesan was chosen rather than Monterey Jack. Cayenne was set at 1/2 tsp.

name: Canadian Hawaiian Pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Set a rack in the middle.
Pat the pizza dough into a 12-inch round on an oiled sheet. Brush the rim with the olive oil.
Spread the pizza sauce over the dough, leaving a small border.
Scatter the mozzarella cheese, then the ham and the pineapple.
Dust the top with the dried oregano.
Bake 14 minutes, until the mozzarella cheese is bubbling and the crust underneath is browned.
Rest 3 minutes, then cut into 8 slices.

attribution.note: No Hawaiian pizza page. Family Pizza and Kid-Friendly Pizza were not assumed to be ham and pineapple.

name: All-Beef Weeknight Chili
steps: Stem and seed the New Mexico chiles. Simmer them in the water for 5 minutes, then steep off the heat for 30 minutes.
Blend the New Mexico chiles with enough of their steeping water to make a smooth puree. Strain out skins and stray seeds.
Cut the beef chuck into 1 1/2-inch chunks. Toss them with the all-purpose flour, the kosher salt, and the black pepper.
Chop the onion. Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion 5 minutes, until translucent.
Brown the beef chuck in batches so the pot is not crowded. Return all the meat to the pot.
Stir in the chile puree and the beef stock, just enough to barely cover the chunks. Bring it to a boil.
Turn the heat to the lowest setting and simmer about 2 1/2 hours, until the beef chuck is easy to cut with a spoon.
Add a splash more beef stock only if the sauce cooks down too far. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).

attribution.note: Reworded from Chili Colorado and scaled to about half for 6 servings (the page uses 5 pounds of chuck). Five chiles stand in for half of nine. The beef is simmered until fork-tender, about 2 1/2 hours after the chile steep.

name: Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork
steps: Stir the water, the pickling salt, and the honey until the salt dissolves. Submerge the pork butt and refrigerate 10 hours. That brine is not included in the 540 minutes.
Pat the pork butt dry. Mix the paprika, the black pepper, the dehydrated lemon peel, the cayenne pepper, the dried rosemary, and the dark brown sugar. Rub the mix over the meat.
Light the apple wood in a smoker and hold the chamber near 210°F (99°C).
Smoke the pork butt 8 to 9 hours, adding apple wood as the fire fades, until a fork twists the meat apart and the center is about 195°F (90°C).
Rest the pork butt 1 hour, then shred it with two forks.
Pile the shredded pork on the hamburger buns.

attribution.note: The page smokes the pork over apple wood until it shreds; the library title still says slow-cooker, but the method follows the smoker. The 8-to-12-hour brine is excluded from the 540 minutes. Apple wood was unmeasured ('several pounds') and set to 3 lb. A 7 lb butt feeds 8 on hamburger buns.

name: Oven BBQ Back Ribs
steps: Pull the membrane off the bone side of the baby-back pork ribs. Coat both sides with the rib rub. Chill the racks for an hour or longer before they go into the oven. That chill is not included in the 180 minutes.
Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C). Seal the hickory and applewood chunks in a foil packet and poke a few holes in the top. Set the packet on a lower rack.

Lay the baby-back pork ribs on a rack over a sheet pan. Roast 2 1/2 hours, brushing with some of the maple barbecue sauce every 45 minutes, until the meat pulls back from the bones and a skewer meets little resistance.
Brush the meaty side with more maple barbecue sauce.
Broil 3 to 4 minutes, watching closely, until the sauce is browned in spots.
Cut into single ribs and pass the remaining maple barbecue sauce at the table.

attribution.note: Oven barbecue instead of the page's smoker and final hot grill. Hickory and applewood chunks smoke from a foil packet in the oven. Rib rub was unmeasured and set to 1/4 cup; maple barbecue sauce was set to 1 cup. The 1-hour rub rest is excluded. Two slabs suit 4 servings. Ribs are cooked until fork-tender, well past 145°F (63°C).

name: Pan-Seared Steak with Mushrooms
steps: Slice the button mushrooms. Mince the garlic and dice the onion.
Brush the new york strip steak with the olive oil and season both sides with the salt and the black pepper.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the new york strip steak about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare, until the center is 130°F (54°C). Rest the steaks 5 minutes.
While the steaks rest, melt the butter in the same skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the garlic in the butter until it smells sweet, about 30 seconds, then add the onion and the button mushrooms.
Toss until the button mushrooms are browned, about 5 minutes.
Set the new york strip steak on plates and spoon the button mushrooms over the top.

attribution.note: Distinct write-up of Steak and Mushrooms, scaled to 2 servings (2 steaks and half the mushrooms, butter, garlic, and onion). Salt, black pepper, and olive oil were unmeasured and set to 3/4 tsp, 1/2 tsp, and 1 tbsp. Steaks are cooked to medium-rare, 130°F (54°C), then rested 5 minutes. Butter means this is not dairy-free.

name: Weeknight Fish & Chips
steps: Heat the vegetable oil to 350°F (180°C) in a deep fryer or heavy pot.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick wedges. Fry them in batches 7 minutes, until crisp and gold. Drain, toss with the sea salt, and keep warm.
Whisk the all-purpose flour, the cornstarch, the salt, and the water into a batter that coats a spoon.
Cut the cod fillets into thick strips and dip them in the batter.
Fry the cod fillets in batches 6 minutes, until the crust is gold and the center of the fish is 145°F (63°C) and opaque.
Drain the cod fillets. Cut the lemon into wedges.
Plate the cod fillets with the potatoes, the lemon, and the parsley. Sprinkle the malt vinegar over the potatoes.

attribution.note: Fish is cooked to 145°F (63°C). Salt in the batter and the finishing sea salt were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp and 1/2 tsp. Water for the batter was set to 3/4 cup. Malt vinegar was set to 2 tbsp. Four fillets and four potatoes suit 4 servings. Cod was chosen from the page's fish options.

name: Nanaimo Bars
steps: Chop the almonds fine. Beat the egg.
Melt the unsalted butter with the granulated sugar and the cocoa over simmering water, stirring until smooth.
Stir the egg into that warm cocoa mix and keep stirring until it thickens slightly, about 2 minutes. Take it off the heat.
Fold in the graham wafer crumbs, the coconut, and the almonds. Press the mix firmly into an ungreased 8-inch square pan.
Beat the custard butter with the cream, the vanilla custard powder, and the icing sugar until the filling is pale and light. Spread it over the crumb layer.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate with the chocolate butter over low heat. Cool until barely warm but still fluid, then pour it over the custard layer.
Chill about 30 minutes, until the chocolate is set. Cut into 16 squares.

attribution.note: Reworded. The page's second butter measure (1/2 cup) is listed as custard butter, and the 2 tbsp for the topping as chocolate butter, so each fat is tracked. Cream is 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp, written as 8 tsp. An 8-inch pan cuts into 16 bars. The chill is included in the 75 minutes.

name: Classic Butter Tarts
steps: Beat the shortening, the butter, and the boiling water until creamy.
Stir in the all-purpose flour, the baking powder, and the salt just until a dough forms. Chill 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and press each into a tart cup.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Chop the walnuts.
Beat the egg, then beat in the brown sugar, the corn syrup, and the melted butter.
Stir in the raisins, the walnuts, the vinegar, the filling salt, and the vanilla extract.
Fill each shell about two-thirds full. Bake 20 minutes, until the pastry edges are light brown.
Cool the tarts in the cups 15 minutes before lifting them out.

attribution.note: Reworded and scaled to half for 12 tarts (the page makes about 24). All-purpose flour was chosen rather than pastry flour, and raisins rather than currants. The page's cornmeal dusting is not an ingredient and was skipped. Pastry salt is 1/4 tsp; the filling uses a pinch listed separately.

name: Skillet Bannock
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Cut the butter into small cubes.
Stir the whole wheat flour, the granulated sugar, the baking soda, and the salt.
Rub in the butter until the mix looks crumbly.
Stir in the buttermilk to make a soft dough. Knead it only a few turns.
Shape a disc about 3 inches thick. Cut a shallow X in the top.
Oil a cast-iron skillet with the oil and set the disc in it.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the center comes out clean.
Cool 8 minutes, then break the loaf into 6 chunks.

attribution.note: Baked in an oiled skillet in the oven rather than on a baking sheet. One loaf from the full flour amount is broken into 6 servings. Oil (1 tbsp) was added to grease the skillet; the page calls for an oiled pan but does not list a separate oil measure.

name: Apple Crisp
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Slice the apples if they are not already sliced, and spread them in a shallow 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle the lemon juice over the apples.
Melt the butter. Stir it with the all-purpose flour, the brown sugar, the rolled oats, the salt, and the cinnamon until crumbly.
Scatter that mix over the apples.
Bake 30 minutes, until the apples are soft when pierced and the topping is browned.
Cool 10 minutes before scooping. Eight portions come from this pan.

attribution.note: Shown as Apple Crisp; the Wikibooks title is Apple Crisp II. The old title named maple, which this page does not list, so the dish is Apple Crisp II. Butter was chosen rather than margarine. A 9-inch pan suits 8 servings.

name: Montreal-Style Bagels with Cream Cheese
steps: Stir the instant yeast and 1 tbsp of the honey into the warm water. Let it stand 5 minutes.
Beat the egg. Mix the bread flour and the salt, then work in the yeast mixture and the egg to a firm dough. Knead 8 minutes.
Cover and let the dough rise 40 minutes, until it is puffy.
Divide into 4 pieces. Roll each into a rope and join the ends to make a ring with a wide hole.
Boil a pot of water with the remaining honey. Boil the rings 45 seconds per side.
Dip the wet tops in the sesame seeds. Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 16 minutes, until deep gold.
Cool 10 minutes. Split the bagels and spread them with the cream cheese.

attribution.note: No Montreal-style bagel page. Plain Bagels is a different method and was not cited as Montreal.

name: Maple Baked Beans
steps: Rinse the dried white beans. Cover them with the water, bring to a boil, boil 5 minutes, then cover and stand off the heat for 1 hour.
Return the beans to a simmer and cook, covered, 45 minutes. Strain them and save the cooking liquid.
Dice the onion. Stir it with the salt, the dry mustard, the black pepper, and the maple syrup, then stir in 2 1/2 cups of the bean liquid.
Slice the bacon and lay it in a casserole. Cover with the beans and pour the maple mixture over them.
Cover and bake at 325°F (165°C) for 2 1/2 hours. Pour in 1/2 cup more bean liquid.
Bake 30 minutes more, still covered.
Melt the butter with the dark brown sugar and pour it over the beans. Bake uncovered until the surface liquid is gone, about 25 minutes.

attribution.note: Reworded. Bacon slices were chosen rather than bacon runoff, so the dish is not vegetarian. Black pepper follows the page's 1/2 tsp figure. The bean pot suits 8 servings. The hour-long stand after the first boil is included in the 330 minutes.

name: Creamy Chicken and Dumplings
steps: Slice the carrot, chop the celery, and chop the onion. Cut the cooked chicken into bite-size pieces.

Put the chicken stock, the cooked chicken, the carrot, the celery, the bay leaf, the onion, the dried thyme, the salt, the black pepper, and the liquid seasoning in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes. The chicken should be hot through, 165°F (74°C).
Stir the all-purpose flour, the baking powder, and the dumpling salt. Cut in the butter until the mix looks grainy.
Stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the simmering stew.
Cook uncovered 5 minutes, then cover and cook 18 minutes, until the dumplings are set on top and no wet dough remains in the center.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.

attribution.note: Chicken is already cooked on the page and is reheated to 165°F (74°C). Salt, black pepper, and liquid seasoning were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp, 1/2 tsp, and 1 tsp. Butter was chosen as the solid fat. Dumpling salt is listed apart from the stew salt. About 2 lb of chicken and 8 cups of stock suit 6 servings.

name: Meatloaf with Pan Gravy
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Mince the garlic. Chop the onion and the celery.
Mix the ground beef, the eggs, the garlic, the salt, the ground allspice, the curry powder, and the Worcestershire sauce.
Work in the onion, the celery, and the cracker crumbs.
Pack the mix into a loaf pan.
Bake 25 minutes, until the top is browned. Tip out any pooled fat.
Spoon the mushroom soup over the loaf.
Bake about 45 minutes more, until the center of the loaf reads 160°F (71°C).
Rest 10 minutes. The mushroom soup on top is the gravy; spoon it over each slice.

attribution.note: Meatloaf is baked to 160°F (71°C). The page's second bake of 1 1/2 to 2 hours was shortened once the center hits that temperature, at 350°F rather than a long 400°F finish. One can of mushroom soup was chosen from the page's 1-to-2 cans and stands in for the pan gravy. Curry powder was only a sprinkle and was set to 1/4 tsp. A 2 lb loaf suits 6 servings.

name: Baked Ziti with Ricotta
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Rub a large baking dish with the olive oil. Chop the basil, the oregano, and the parsley. Grate the mozzarella and the Parmesan cheese if they are not already grated.
Beat the egg into the ricotta with the basil, the oregano, the parsley, half the mozzarella, half the Parmesan cheese, the salt, and the black pepper.
Boil the ziti in salted water until it still has a firm center, about 8 minutes. Drain it well.
Toss the ziti with the marinara sauce and the red pepper flakes. Fold in the ricotta mixture and spread it in the dish.
Top with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan cheese, then the bread crumbs.
Bake 20 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and the bread crumbs are golden.
Rest 5 minutes before serving 8 portions.

attribution.note: Ricotta is on the page and is included. Salt and black pepper were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp and 1/2 tsp. Olive oil for the dish was not listed; 1 tbsp was added so the pasta does not stick. Optional red pepper flakes were kept as a pinch. One pound of ziti suits 8 servings.

name: Country Sausage Gravy & Biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Warm the biscuits on a sheet for 10 minutes so they are hot when the gravy is ready.
Brown the breakfast sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes.
Scoop the breakfast sausage into a bowl and leave the drippings in the skillet.
Add the bacon grease and melt it over medium-low heat. Whisk in the all-purpose flour and cook 1 minute.
Pour in the milk slowly, whisking. Bring it to a gentle bubble and stir for about 10 minutes, until the gravy coats a spoon.
Stir the breakfast sausage, the salt, and the black pepper back into the gravy. Take it off the heat and let it stand 1 minute.
Split the biscuits and ladle the gravy over them.

attribution.note: Reworded. The page tells you to bake cut biscuits but lists no dough ingredients, so 6 ready biscuits are warmed and the gravy uses only the listed sausage, bacon grease, flour, milk, salt, and pepper. Black pepper follows the page's 1/4 tbsp (3/4 tsp). Sausage is cooked to 160°F (71°C). The batch suits 6 servings.

name: Loaded Baked Potato Soup
steps: Chop the bacon and dice the onion, the potatoes, and the chives. Mince the garlic.
Fry the bacon over medium heat until crisp, about 6 minutes. Drain it on a towel and leave a little fat in the pan.
Add the butter and the onion. Cook 2 minutes, then add the garlic and cook until the onion is soft, about 3 minutes more.
Stir in the all-purpose flour and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in the chicken broth a little at a time. Add the potatoes and the milk. Simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Season with the salt and the black pepper. Stir in half the bacon, cover, and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the cheddar cheese until it melts. Ladle the soup and top it with the remaining bacon and the chives.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).

attribution.note: Reworded from Cheesy Potato Soup. Bacon, butter, onion, broth, potatoes, milk, cheese, chives, salt, and pepper were unmeasured; amounts were set for 6 servings. Sour cream is named in the method but not in the ingredient list, so it was left out. Chicken broth means the soup is not vegetarian.

name: Tater Tot Hotdish
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). The page never names an oven temperature; 375°F is used here.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, until it reaches 160°F (71°C), about 10 minutes. Drain the fat.
Stir the cream of mushroom soup into the ground beef.
Spread that mix in a casserole dish.
Cover the surface with a single layer of the tater tots.
Bake 60 minutes, until the tater tots are deep gold and the sauce is bubbling at the edges.
Rest 5 minutes before serving 6 portions.

attribution.note: Reworded. Cream of mushroom soup was chosen rather than cream of chicken. Ground beef is cooked to 160°F (71°C). The page says about half a bag of tater tots, written here as 1/2 package, with 1 1/2 lb beef from the page's 1-to-2 lb range for 6 servings. Oven temperature was missing and set to 375°F.

name: Chicken and Wild Rice Casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Dice the onion, the celery, and the mushrooms. Mince the garlic. Cut the chicken breast into 1-inch pieces.
Rinse the wild rice. Simmer it in 3 cups of the chicken broth for 35 minutes, until the grains split and are tender. Drain any extra liquid.
Melt the butter in a wide pan. Cook the onion, the celery, the mushrooms, and the garlic 6 minutes, until softened.
Season the chicken breast with the salt, the black pepper, and the dried thyme. Add it to the pan and cook until the pieces read 165°F (74°C), about 8 minutes.
Sprinkle on the all-purpose flour and stir 1 minute. Pour in the remaining chicken broth and the milk. Simmer until the sauce thickens, about 4 minutes.
Fold in the wild rice. Spread the mix in a greased 9-by-13-inch dish.
Bake 20 minutes, until the edges bubble. Rest 5 minutes. This pan serves 8.

attribution.note: No chicken and wild rice casserole page.

name: Beef and Noodle Skillet Supper
steps: Boil the water with the salt. Cook the macaroni until it still has a little bite, about 8 minutes. Drain it.
While the macaroni cooks, scatter the garlic salt and the minced onion in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the ground beef and break it up. Cook until no pink remains and it reads 160°F (71°C), about 10 minutes. Drain extra fat.
Stir in the tomato soup and cook 2 minutes.
Fold in the drained macaroni and cook 1 minute more so the noodles take up the sauce.
Spoon the macaroni and ground beef into 6 bowls.

attribution.note: Ground beef is cooked to 160°F (71°C). Scaled about 1 1/2 times for 6 servings from the page's 1 cup pasta and 1 pound beef. Garlic salt and minced onion were only 'a sprinkle' and were set to 1 1/2 tsp and 3 tbsp. Water and salt for the pasta boil were added because the method needs them; set to 6 cups and 1 tsp.

name: Garlic Shrimp Spaghetti
steps: Boil the spaghetti until it is tender with a little bite, about 9 minutes.
Slice the garlic. Chop the parsley. Juice the lemon.
Melt the butter in a wide skillet over medium heat. Stir the garlic for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and cook about 6 minutes, turning once, until they are pink and the thickest piece reads 145°F (63°C).
Season with the salt and the black pepper. Stir in the lemon juice, the red chile flakes, and the parsley.
Drain the spaghetti and toss it in the skillet until it is coated with the butter and shrimp juices.
Divide the spaghetti and shrimp among 4 plates.

attribution.note: Reworded. Shrimp are cooked to 145°F (63°C). Butter is in the sauce, so the dish is not dairy-free. Amounts match the page for 4 servings.

name: Taco Casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Tear the tortillas into bits.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium heat until it reaches 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes. Drain the fat and return the meat to the skillet.
Pour in the tomato sauce. Sprinkle over the taco seasoning, then the garlic powder and the chili powder.
Simmer 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Fold the tortilla bits and the shredded cheese into the meat. Spread the mix in a casserole dish.
Bake 20 minutes, until the shredded cheese is bubbling and the edges are browned.
Rest 5 minutes, then scoop out 4 portions.

attribution.note: The duplicate turkey taco skillet was replaced with this beef taco casserole. Ground beef is cooked to 160°F (71°C). Tortillas and cheese mean it is not gluten-free or dairy-free. The page's full batch suits about 4 servings. Chili powder and garlic powder stay at the page's 3 tbsp each.

name: Baked Chicken Breasts
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat the chicken breasts dry.
Brush both sides of the chicken breasts with the olive oil.
Season both sides with the salt, the black pepper, and the lemon zest.
Lay the chicken breasts in a 13-by-9-inch pan.
Bake until the thickest breast reads 165°F (74°C), about 22 to 28 minutes.
Move the chicken breasts to a plate and rest 5 minutes before serving.

attribution.note: The lemon-herb sheet pan had a twin; this is the baked-breast dish. Salt, black pepper, olive oil, and lemon zest were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp, 1/2 tsp, 1 tbsp, and 1 tsp. Chicken is baked to 165°F (74°C). Four breasts suit 4 servings.

name: Pork Stir-Fry with Peppers
steps: Slice the pork loin thin. Slice the bell peppers and the onion. Mince the garlic and the fresh ginger.
Stir the soy sauce, the black pepper, the cornstarch, and the water into a thin slurry.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Stir-fry the pork loin 3 minutes, until it is browned and the slices read 145°F (63°C). Scoop it out and rest it 3 minutes.
Add the bell peppers and the onion to the pan. Stir-fry 3 minutes, until the edges char and the peppers are still crisp.
Return the pork loin with the garlic and the fresh ginger. Toss 30 seconds.
Pour in the soy sauce slurry and toss until it glosses the pork loin and peppers, about 30 seconds. Serve in 4 bowls.

attribution.note: No pork-and-pepper stir-fry page. Steak and Pepper Stir-Fry is beef.

name: Caprese Chicken Cutlets
steps: Pound the chicken breasts to about 1/2 inch thick. Season them with the salt and the black pepper.
Slice the tomatoes and the mozzarella. Tear the basil. Mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the chicken breasts 4 minutes per side, until the center reads 165°F (74°C).
In the last minute, scatter the garlic over the chicken breasts, then top each with tomato slices and mozzarella.
Cover the skillet 1 minute, until the mozzarella softens.
Strew the basil over the chicken breasts and rest 3 minutes before serving.

attribution.note: No caprese chicken cutlet page. Chicken Parmesan is r191.

name: Sausage and Broccoli Pasta
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil with half the salt. Cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the garlic. Remove the Italian sausage from its casings.
Boil the pasta until tender with a little bite, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Drain and save 1/2 cup of the pasta water.
Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the Italian sausage, breaking it up, until it reaches 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and the red pepper flakes and stir 30 seconds.
Toss in the pasta, the broccoli, the remaining salt, and a splash of the pasta water.
Take the pan off the heat and toss with the Parmesan cheese until the noodles look glossy.
Divide the pasta, Italian sausage, and broccoli among 4 bowls.

attribution.note: No sausage-and-broccoli pasta page.

name: Grilled Sliders
steps: Heat the oven to 250°F (120°C) and a grill to medium, about 350°F (175°C).
Split the hamburger buns and toast them in the oven about 8 minutes. Set them aside.
Stir the salt, the black pepper, the garlic powder, and the dried rosemary.
Mix the ground chuck with the ground sirloin. Press the meat on a lined sheet into an even slab and cut 24 equal squares.
Brush both sides of the squares with the olive oil and season them with the spice mix.
Grill the patties 3 to 4 minutes per side, until the center of a patty reads 160°F (71°C).
Spread the mayonnaise on the hamburger buns. Put two patties in each bun so you have 12 sliders.

attribution.note: Reworded. The old title named caramelized onions, which this page does not list, so the dish is Grilled Sliders. Scaled about 1 1/2 times for 12 servings (24 small patties, 12 buns). Olive oil and mayonnaise were unmeasured and set to 1 1/2 tbsp and 3/4 cup. Ground beef is cooked to 160°F (71°C).

name: Big-Batch Baked Macaroni
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grate the cheese.
Boil the elbow macaroni in a large pot of water with the salt until tender, about 8 minutes. Drain it.
Warm the milk and stir in the cheese until you have a smooth sauce. Add a splash more milk only if it is pasty.
Melt the butter in a wide pot. Stir in the elbow macaroni until every piece is coated.
Crack in the eggs and stir until they disappear into the hot pasta. Fold in the cheese sauce, the dried parsley, and the dried oregano.
Spread the mix in a large greased baking dish.
Bake 25 minutes, until the top is set and the edges bubble. Rest 5 minutes. This pan serves 12.

attribution.note: Big-batch bake from this macaroni and cheese, which the page finishes on the stove. Baking at 350°F for 25 minutes is the change. Scaled about 3 times for 12 servings from 8 ounces of macaroni. Salt was unmeasured and set to 1 1/2 tsp after scaling. The page's dash of parsley and oregano was set to 1/2 tsp each before the scale, so 1 1/2 tsp each here.

name: Sheet-Pan Fajita Feast
steps: Juice 2 of the limes. Chop the green onions. Blend the olive oil, the soy sauce, that lime juice, the red pepper flakes, the cumin, the green onions, and the dark brown sugar until smooth.
Seal the skirt steak in a bag with the marinade and refrigerate at least 1 hour, or up to a day. That soak is not included in the 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Cut the onions into wedges and slice the red bell peppers and the green bell peppers. Toss them with the vegetable oil on a sheet pan.
Roast the vegetables 12 minutes, until they soften and brown in spots.

Lift the skirt steak from the marinade, discard the marinade, and lay the steak on a second hot sheet. Roast until the thickest part is 145°F (63°C), about 10 to 14 minutes for medium. Rest 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in the oven for 3 minutes. Cut the remaining limes into wedges.
Slice the skirt steak thinly across the grain. Serve with the peppers and onions, the tortillas, the salsa fresca, the guacamole, and the lime wedges. This batch feeds 8.

attribution.note: Sheet-pan feast instead of the page's charcoal grill, scaled as the full 2.25 lb steak for 8 servings. The marinade of at least 1 hour is excluded from the 45 minutes. Steak is cooked to 145°F (63°C) and rested 3 minutes. Tortillas, salsa fresca, and guacamole were unmeasured and set to 8 tortillas, 1 cup salsa, and 1 cup guacamole. Soy sauce and tortillas mean this is not gluten-free.

name: Italian Meatballs
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Mince the garlic. Grate the Parmesan cheese.

Mix the ground veal, the dried oregano, the dried parsley, the garlic, the eggs, the breadcrumbs, the Parmesan cheese, the salt, and the black pepper. Work the mix with your hands until it holds together.
Roll it into bite-size meatballs.
Film a large skillet with the olive oil over medium heat. Brown the meatballs uncovered about 3 minutes, then roll them and brown 3 minutes more.
Move the meatballs to a baking sheet.
Bake 22 minutes, until the center of a meatball reads 160°F (71°C).
Rest 5 minutes. This batch makes enough for 8 servings, without rolls because the page lists none.

attribution.note: The old title was meatball subs, but the page has no bread, so the dish is Italian Meatballs. Scaled about 2 times for 8 servings from 500 g of veal. The page's 125 g of breadcrumbs was taken as 1 cup per 500 g (the printed 1/4 cup conflicts with that weight), so 2 cups here. Salt, black pepper, and olive oil were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp, 1/2 tsp, and 2 tbsp. Veal meatballs are baked to 160°F (71°C).

name: Slow-Cooker Beef Barbacoa
steps: Cut the beef chuck into 3 large chunks. Chop the onion and mince the garlic. Mince the chipotle chiles.
Stir the onion, the garlic, the chipotle chiles, the adobo sauce, the ground cumin, the dried oregano, the ground cloves, the lime juice, the beef broth, the salt, and the black pepper.
Put the beef chuck and the bay leaves in a slow cooker and pour the sauce over the meat.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef chuck shreds when pressed with a fork.
Discard the bay leaves. Shred the beef chuck in the sauce.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).
Taste and leave it juicy. This pot serves 8.

attribution.note: No barbacoa page. Cochinita pibil is a different braise.

name: Crockpot Chicken Tikka Masala
steps: Chop the garlic and the onions. Chop the plum tomatoes and the green chiles. Chop the cilantro. Cut the chicken tikka into bite-size pieces if it is still in large chunks.
Warm the mustard seed oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic and the onions until browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the curry paste and the tandoori masala paste with the water. Scrape this base into a slow cooker.
Add the chicken tikka, the plum tomatoes, the malt vinegar, the tomato paste, and the green chiles.
Cover and cook on low for 3 1/2 hours, until the sauce is thick and the chicken tikka is hot through at 165°F (74°C).
Stir in the single cream, the garam masala, and the cilantro. Cover 10 minutes more.
Spoon into 6 bowls and scatter a little extra cilantro on top if any remains.

attribution.note: Slow cooker instead of the page's wok simmer. The chicken tikka is already cooked and is held at 165°F (74°C) in the sauce. Onions were kept. Two green chiles were chosen from the page's range. Water (1/4 cup) was added because the page loosens the pastes with a little water. A 1.5 lb batch suits 6 servings. Malt vinegar was chosen rather than tamarind.

name: Slow-Cooker Lentil Curry
steps: Rinse the red split lentils. Put them in a slow cooker with the water, the salt, and the bay leaf.
Peel and cube the potatoes. Toss them with the turmeric, the cayenne pepper, the olive oil, and the margarine.
Fry the potatoes in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes, until the edges color.
Add the potatoes to the slow cooker with the diced tomatoes, the garam masala, and the sugar.
Cover and cook on low for 4 1/2 hours, until the potatoes are soft and the red split lentils have broken down.
Discard the bay leaf. Stir and ladle 8 bowls.

attribution.note: Slow cooker instead of the page's stovetop pot. Margarine was chosen rather than butter, and sugar rather than honey, so the curry stays dairy-free and vegan. The full pot suits 8 servings. The 300 minutes include the long slow cook.

name: Black Bean Chili
steps: Cover the dried black beans with 8 cups of the water and soak them overnight. Drain and discard that soaking water. That soak is not included in the 210 minutes.
Cover the beans with 4 cups of the water, bring them to a boil, then simmer 2 hours until they are tender. Keep the bean liquid.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Chop the chipotle chile and the ancho chile.
Heat the corn oil in a large pot. Cook the onion 3 minutes, until tender.
Add the garlic, the chipotle chile, the ancho chile, the cumin, the paprika, the dried oregano, the sea salt, the cayenne pepper, and the wine vinegar. Cook 8 minutes.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, the tomato puree, and the last 4 cups of the water. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add the beans and their liquid. Simmer 1 hour, until the chili is thick. This pot serves 10.

attribution.note: Vague set-and-forget chili was replaced with black bean chili. The overnight soak is excluded from the 210 minutes. Optional sour cream was left off so the chili stays dairy-free and vegan. Sea salt follows the page's 3/4 tbsp. The dried-bean pot suits 10 servings.

name: Honey BBQ Hot Wings
steps: Pat the chicken wingettes dry. Toss them with the salt, the black pepper, and the oil.
Pile the chicken wingettes in a slow cooker, cover, and cook on high for 2 1/2 hours, until the thickest wingette reads 165°F (74°C).
Stir the tomato paste, the honey, the cider vinegar, and the hot sauce in a small saucepan.
Boil that sauce over medium-high heat until it reduces to about 10 tbsp, roughly 8 minutes.
Take the sauce off the heat and let it stand 5 minutes.
Drain extra liquid from the slow cooker. Toss the chicken wingettes with the sauce.
Spoon onto a platter for 6 people.

attribution.note: The old title named garlic, which this page does not list, so the dish is Honey BBQ Hot Wings. Slow cooker instead of the page's deep fryer, disclosed here. Chicken is cooked to 165°F (74°C). Salt, black pepper, and oil were unmeasured; set to 1 tsp, 1/2 tsp, and 2 tbsp for the cooker rather than a full pot of frying oil. Twenty-four wingettes suit 6 servings.

name: Grilled Salmon with Lemon Butter Sauce
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat the salmon fillets dry.
Brush the salmon fillets with the olive oil and season them with the salt and the black pepper.
Lay the salmon fillets skin side down in one baking pan.
Bake until the thickest fillet reads 145°F (63°C) and the flesh flakes, about 14 minutes.
Juice the lemon. Mash the lemon juice into the unsalted butter, then melt that mix in a small saucepan over medium heat, about 3 minutes.
Spoon the lemon butter over the salmon fillets and serve the four pieces from the same pan.

attribution.sourceTitle: Cookbook:Grilled Salmon with Lemon Butter Sauce
attribution.note: The old title named garlic, which this page does not list, so the name follows the page. One-pan bake at 400°F instead of the page's charcoal grill. Salmon is cooked to 145°F (63°C). Salt, black pepper, and olive oil were unmeasured and set to 1 tsp, 1/2 tsp, and 1 tbsp. Butter means the dish is not dairy-free. About 24 ounces of salmon suits 4 servings.

sources.title: Cookbook:Grilled Salmon with Lemon Butter Sauce

name: Sweet Italian Sausage Skillet
steps: Boil the rotini until tender, about 8 minutes. Drain it. Slice the sweet Italian sausage into coins. Shred the provolone.
Heat the cooking oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the sweet Italian sausage 6 minutes, until the centers read 160°F (71°C). Pour off the extra fat.
Stir in the stewed tomatoes with their juice, the tomato paste, the chicken broth, and the drained green beans.
Bring the skillet to a boil, then cover and simmer 10 minutes, until the green beans are tender.
Stir in the rotini and heat 1 minute.
Scatter the provolone over the skillet and cover 1 minute, until it melts. This pan serves 4.

attribution.note: Same sausage-and-peppers page as another id, written here as the skillet supper. The old title named peppers; the page uses green beans, so the name is Sweet Italian Sausage Skillet. Provolone was chosen rather than mozzarella. The page lists both 5 oz and 410 g for the tomatoes and the beans; 14 oz was used to follow the gram figure. Sausage is cooked to 160°F (71°C). The batch suits 4 servings.

name: One-Pan Greek Chicken and Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut the potatoes and the onion into wedges. Mince the garlic. Juice the lemon and keep the rind.
Toss the potatoes and the onion on a sheet pan with half the olive oil, half the salt, and half the black pepper.
Stir the remaining olive oil with the garlic, the dried oregano, the remaining salt, the remaining black pepper, and the lemon juice. Rub that over the chicken thighs.
Nest the chicken thighs among the potatoes. Scatter the lemon rind over the pan.
Roast 40 minutes, until the potatoes are browned and the thickest chicken thigh reads 165°F (74°C).
Rest 5 minutes. This pan serves 6.

attribution.note: No Greek chicken and potatoes page. Greek Chicken Wrap is a wrap.

name: Shrimp and Orzo One-Pot
steps: Peel the shrimp if needed. Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and chop the parsley. Juice the lemon.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 4 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds.
Pour in the orzo and stir 1 minute so the grains look glossy.
Add the chicken broth, the diced tomatoes, the salt, and the black pepper. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 10 minutes, until the orzo is almost tender.
Nest the shrimp in the orzo, cover, and cook 4 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and the thickest piece reads 145°F (63°C).
Stir in the lemon juice and the parsley. Rest 2 minutes off the heat. This pot serves 4.

attribution.note: No shrimp and orzo page. Orzo Salad is a salad and is used for r45.

name: Apple Glazed Pork Chops
steps: Rub the grill seasoning over the pork chops. Refrigerate 30 minutes. That rest is included in the 45 minutes.
Stir the apple cider, the cider vinegar, and the Worcestershire sauce in a small saucepan. Boil over medium heat until the mix has reduced by about a third, about 8 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Lay the pork chops on a sheet pan.
Brush the pork chops with some of the cider glaze. Roast 8 minutes.
Turn the pork chops, brush them again, and roast until the center of each chop is 145°F (63°C), about 8 minutes more.
Rest the pork chops 3 minutes. Spoon the remaining glaze over them.

attribution.note: Sheet-pan roast instead of the page's grill, called out against the other apple-chop write-up. The old title named apple pieces; the page uses apple cider, so the name is Apple Glazed Pork Chops. Grill seasoning was unmeasured and set to 1 tbsp. Pork chops are cooked to 145°F (63°C) and rested 3 minutes. The 30-minute seasoning rest is included. Four chops suit 4 servings.

name: Grilled Marinated Flank Steak
steps: Crack the peppercorns. Stir them with the salt, the cayenne pepper, and the smoked paprika.
Brush the flank steak all over with the Dijon mustard. Press the spice mix into the meat and let it stand 20 minutes. That stand is the marinade and is included in the 45 minutes.
Heat a grill to high. Mark the flank steak on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Lower the heat to medium and keep turning until the center reads 140°F (60°C) for medium, about 6 minutes more.
Rest the flank steak uncovered for 7 minutes.
Slice it very thin across the grain. One pound serves 4.

attribution.note: Marinated with mustard and spices, then grilled. Salt was unmeasured and set to 1 tsp. Dijon mustard was unmeasured and set to 2 tbsp. Cooked to medium, 140°F (60°C), then rested 7 minutes before slicing. A 1 lb steak suits 4 servings.

name: BBQ Chicken Drumsticks
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Stir the paprika, the onion powder, the chilli powder, and the salt.
Pat the chicken drumsticks dry.
Rub the chicken drumsticks with the olive oil, then with the spice mix, covering every side.
Set the chicken drumsticks in a baking dish with a little space between them.
Bake until the skin is browned and the thickest drumstick reads 165°F (74°C), about 35 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes. Six drumsticks serve 6.

attribution.note: Chicken is roasted to 165°F (74°C). The page's roughly 25 minutes was extended so the drumsticks reach that temperature. The spice rub is the barbecue seasoning; there is no separate sauce on the page. Six drumsticks suit 6 servings. This is an oven roast, so it is not filed as a grill recipe.

name: Weeknight Minestrone
steps: Cut the vegetables into bite-size pieces. Boil them 3 minutes in water seasoned with the salt, then drain.
Melt the butter in a soup pot over medium heat and fry the vegetables 4 minutes, until they pick up a little color.
Pour in the vegetable stock. Lower the heat and keep it at a bare simmer.
In a separate pot, simmer the rice in 2 cups of the vegetable stock until the grains are fully soft, about 18 minutes.
Stir that rice and its liquid back into the vegetables.
Stir in the minestrone seasoning and simmer 5 minutes.
Ladle 6 bowls and pass the grated cheese separately.

attribution.note: Reworded. The page lists vegetables, butter, stock, rice, seasoning, and grated cheese without amounts or a vegetable list. Amounts were set for 6 servings, and the rice was raised from 4 oz to 6 oz. Vegetable stock was chosen so the soup stays meatless. Salt (1 tsp) was added for the blanching water.

name: Creamy Tomato Tortellini Soup
steps: Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Melt the butter in a soup pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and the Italian seasoning and stir 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the vegetable broth, the salt, and the black pepper. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add the cheese tortellini and cook until the pasta is tender, about 7 minutes, or follow the package if it asks for less.
Stir in the heavy cream and the spinach. Simmer 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the soup is hot.
Ladle the tomato soup and cheese tortellini into 4 bowls.
